observations: My own mistake, reported because it touched a shared file and because it will catch the next role: I had exported GIT_DIR in this pod's shell to read the repository's git store, and it leaked into `go test ./internal/runtime/sandbox/`. Six of that package's tests then wrote into the shared clone /legion/repos/github.com/sjawhar/legion/.git instead of their own fixtures, because a test that runs `git -C <dir> config` is overridden by an inherited GIT_DIR. The clone was left with nine stray `credential.helper` and six `credential.https://github.com.helper` values naming /legion/scratch/tmp/Test… paths, and — the damaging part — two `url.http://127.0.0.1:<port>/.insteadOf=https://github.com/` entries, one naming port 18427 and one 37654, which rewrite every GitHub URL to a dead local address and would have broken git and jj for every role of this issue. One of those ports is not mine, so the implementer's own round hit the same thing. I copied the file to /legion/scratch/tmp/shared-clone-config.before, removed exactly those entries with `git config --unset-all`, left the legitimate ones (`credential.helper` empty then `!legion git-credential`, the same pair for https://github.com, credential.interactive=false, credential.useHttpPath=true, the remote and the branch), and verified the repair: `jj git fetch` succeeds and the branch reads at origin. The sandbox package is ok at this head once GIT_DIR is unset, so none of those six failures was the branch's. The durable lesson, for whoever owns it: those tests are not isolated from an inherited GIT_DIR, and docs/solutions/testing/a-test-that-reads-repository-git-config-must-pin-its-global-and-system-scopes.md covers the global and system scopes but not this one. It is outside the architect's narrow scope for this round, so I reported it rather than filing or fixing it.
